title: International remittance transfers - federal disclosures
facts: Federal Regulation E provides protections for many consumer electronic transfers from the United States to recipients abroad.
Covered remittance providers generally must disclose information including the amount transferred, certain fees and taxes, exchange rate where applicable, and the amount expected to be received.
Consumers generally receive a receipt containing additional information such as availability date and error-resolution rights.
Coverage depends on whether the transaction and provider meet the federal remittance-transfer definitions and thresholds.
